title: embeddings-regression-canary-runbook-draft
summary: Canary rollout of model v3.2.0 caused a measurable regression in embedding quality for semantic similarity queries. A subset of traffic (canary) saw cosine similarity drops and retrieval precision fall ~18% vs baseline. Initial indicators pointed at token-to-embedding alignment shifts after weight conversion and a tokenizer offset change in the packaging step.
detection_metrics: Primary signal: downstream kNN precision@10 dropped from 0.83 -> 0.68 on canary traffic. Secondary: mean pairwise cosine similarity of control prompts decreased by ~0.12. Latency unaffected. Alert triggered by embedding-regression-alert rule when precision@10 delta > 0.10 for 5m.
timeline:
2024-10-22 09:05 UTC - Canary rollout to 1% starts for model v3.2.0
2024-10-22 09:12 UTC - Embedding precision alert fires (precision@10 drop > 0.10)
2024-10-22 09:14 UTC - On-call SRE (Sarah) acknowledges incident
2024-10-22 09:20 UTC - Canary traffic reduced to 0.1% while investigating
2024-10-22 09:35 UTC - Engineers observe embedding vector drift against stored indexed vectors
2024-10-22 09:50 UTC - Quick diff of model packaging artifacts shows tokenizer config changed (offset handling) in build step PR-embed-quant-fix
2024-10-22 10:05 UTC - Rollback initiated for canary (model pegged back to v3.1.7 for affected routes)
2024-10-22 10:18 UTC - Precision metrics return to baseline on canary
2024-10-22 11:00 UTC - Incident declared contained; follow-up actions assigned
root_cause: During the packaging/quantization pipeline for v3.2.0 we applied an updated token-offset normalization (intended to align legacy tokenizer behavior with an experimental tokenizer fix) but the change was not backward-compatible with the index-building script used by the retrieval pipeline. The mismatch caused token boundaries to shift for a subset of inputs, which changed embedding inputs and produced vectors that no longer aligned with existing vector indexes. Two contributing factors: (1) the build step altered tokenizer byte offsets but artifact naming did not reflect the tokenizer version; (2) the canary policy allowed mixed index/model compatibility without a compatibility gate.
immediate_mitigation:
1) Reduced canary percentage to 0.1% within 8 minutes of detection.
2) Rolled canary routes back to v3.1.7 (previous stable).
3) Disabled automated index-rewrite jobs triggered by model changes.
4) Set temporary circuit-breaker on rebuilds for affected tenants.
rollback_steps:
1) Identify all routes using model v3.2.0 via routing table query.
2) For each route, set model override to v3.1.7 and verify deployment success.
3) Monitor embedding precision and cosine similarity dashboards for 15 minutes post-rollback.
4) Re-enable index rewrite jobs only after compatibility confirmed.
5) Document the artifact SHA and tokenizer config used in the rollback in incident ticket.
runbook_draft:
Purpose: give SREs a repeatable checklist for detecting and remediating tokenizer/embedding regressions during rollouts.
Pre-rollout checks: 
- Confirm tokenizer config version is pinned in model metadata and artifact manifest.
- Ensure packaging pipeline outputs 'tokenizer-version' key and documented offset policy.
- Run synthetic embedding regression tests (anchor prompts + index) as part of CI with min precision@10 threshold.
Detection knobs: 
- Embedding precision@10, mean cosine delta, and downstream retrieval CTR.
- Canary thresholds: trigger if precision@10 drop > 0.08 sustained for 3 minutes.
On-call playbook: 
- Acknowledge alert and read this runbook.
- Cut canary traffic by half immediately; if still falling, drop to 0.1% and pause rollout.
- Check packaging artifact manifest for tokenizer-version mismatch.
- If mismatch found, tag artifact as incompatible and rollback canary.
- Start postmortem ticket and gather logs, packaging artifacts, and index metadata.
Verification before re-rollout: 
- Rebuild vector index with new tokenizer OR restore tokenizer to previous spec.
- Run end-to-end retrieval regression tests and a 24-hour canary with additional telemetry sampling.
postmortem_actions: Add tokenizer-version to mandatory artifact metadata (CON-4823)
Block rollouts where tokenizer-version differs from last index build
Add CI synthetic embedding tests for packaging changes
Improve canary policy to include index compatibility gate
Create a lightweight index-compatibility shim for temporary fallbacks
notes_to_oncall: If you see embedding precision drop without latency change, suspect tokenizer or input preprocessing first. Check recent packaging PRs and packaging pipeline logs. Preserve all packaging artifacts (tarball + manifest) for at least 72 hours. If rollback completed, keep monitoring for 60 minutes before declaring stable. Escalate to Applied ML if root cause touches model conversion.
open_questions:
1) Why did the packaging pipeline accept tokenizer offset change without a compatibility flag?
2) Do any other models share the same index-building script that could be impacted?
3) Should we version index metadata separately from model artifacts?
final_notes: Draft runbook aims to reduce time-to-detect and provide clear rollback steps for tokenizer-related embedding regressions. Next: get Applied ML sign-off on compatibility criteria and land CON-4823 before next rollout. Schedule a short postmortem review with SRE, Applied ML, and Packaging teams within 1 week.
body:
Incident writeup (SRE draft) - embedding regression during canary rollout

Context:
We rolled model v3.2.0 (packaged with an experimental tokenizer offset normalization) to 1% canary traffic on 2024-10-22. Within ~7 minutes the embedding precision alarm fired. Canary traffic was quickly reduced and canary routes rolled back. The regression did not cause latency or error-rate issues, but semantic retrieval quality dropped significantly for affected tenants.

Technical notes:
- The tokenizer change affected token boundary computation for certain multi-byte unicode sequences; this subtly changed tokenization granularity for ~4% of queries in our synthetic corpus.
- Embedding model expects consistent tokenization to produce vectors that align with pre-built vector indexes. When tokenization is inconsistent, nearest-neighbor retrieval returns different neighbors and precision drops.
- The packaging pipeline accepted the change because artifact manifests were not validated against index metadata.

Suggested immediate policy updates:
- Enforce tokenizer-version equality check between model artifact and most recent index build metadata; fail rollouts when mismatch found.
- Add a canary compatibility gate in the control-plane that runs a fast index-compatibility probe (sample N=500 queries) before releasing more than 1% traffic.

Appendix (on-call checklist):
- Acknowledge alert in pagerduty.
- Run `grpc get-routes --model v3.2.0` to enumerate routes.
- Run diagnostic embedding job `tools/emb-diff --artifact v3.2.0 --baseline v3.1.7 --samples 1000`.
- If diagnostic shows mean cosine delta > 0.08, set route overrides to v3.1.7 and disable index rebuilds.
- Attach packaging manifest and logs to incident ticket.
